tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The README explains that Treetracker Web Map shows the location and details of trees tracked by Greenstand. It is the starting point for setup and the vocabulary used in the tour. The package manifest shows the Next.js, React and MUI stack.

tour.title: App Shell Entry Point
tour.description: _app.js is the Next.js shell that wraps every page. It sets up the MUI emotion cache, theme, analytics and the global providers. Every later step runs inside this shell.
tour.languageLesson: Next.js _app.js wraps each page component, so providers placed there are shared across all routes.

tour.title: Routing with Pages
tour.description: Next.js maps files under src/pages to routes. The home page hosts the global map. Dynamic files such as [treeid].js and [planterid].js serve tree, planter, organization, wallet and token details.
tour.languageLesson: Square brackets in a Next.js file name create a dynamic route segment.

tour.title: Models and API Client
tour.description: The model layer talks to the backend. api.js and apiPaths.js build requests, MapModel.js wraps the map, and runtimeEnv.js reads environment values at runtime. The pages from Step 3 call these to fetch their data.

tour.title: State, Contexts and Hooks
tour.description: React contexts hold theme, drawer, config and map state. Custom hooks such as the global hooks wrap browser features like mobile detection and fullscreen. They let the components in the next steps stay small.

tour.title: Map Home and Layouts
tour.description: Home and the Layout components assemble the global map screen with desktop, mobile and embed variants. CustomWorldMap renders the map using the models and state from Steps 4 and 5.

tour.title: Navigation and Search
tour.description: Navbar, Link and the search components let users move around and find trees or planters. Link is one of the most reused components in the code base.

tour.title: Detail UI Components
tour.description: Cards, timelines, share buttons and image viewers render tree and planter details on the pages from Step 3. ErrorBoundary protects them from render failures.

tour.title: Theming and Design Sandbox
tour.description: The theme playground and DesignSandbox let designers tune colors and typography live. The admin theme page uses the theme context from Step 5.

tour.title: Testing Strategy
tour.description: Jest and MSW mocks cover units and data, and Cypress covers components and end-to-end flows. test-utils.js is the most reused file in the repo and gives tests the same providers as the app.

tour.title: API Documentation
tour.description: The OpenAPI spec and example payloads describe the backend contract that the API client in Step 4 consumes.
tour.languageLesson: OpenAPI YAML declares paths, parameters and response schemas, so it doubles as documentation and a contract.

tour.title: Containers and Kubernetes
tour.description: The Dockerfile packages the Next.js app into an image. Kustomize bases and overlays in the deployment folders set up each environment with shared manifests and small per-environment patches.
tour.languageLesson: Kustomize overlays patch a base manifest, so environments differ only by small diffs.

tour.title: CI/CD Workflows
tour.description: GitHub Actions run checks on pull requests, build images and deploy to the dev, test and prod channels. This ties the whole tour together by shipping the app from Step 12.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions use on triggers, jobs and steps to automate build and release.
